Subject: VPC connectivity - post-call recap and next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for a productive call today — appreciate you walking through FinPay's expected traffic patterns and security constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of needs:
- VPC-private connectivity from FinPay to Redwood endpoints (VPC endpoints / interface endpoints preferred)
- IP allowlist for any egress to third-party services and for management plane callbacks
- Egress/DNS requirements: need to keep DNS resolution in your VPC and ensure mTLS-enabled egress for callbacks
- Auth & SDK: service-account style auth for server-to-server calls; SDK guidance for node/python + examples
- Embeddings / reranker: want to use embeddings for semantic search (100M docs initially) and a reranker for top-k precision

What we (Redwood) will provide / validate:
- Recommended VPC endpoint configuration and security group rules (attached arch diagram)
- IP ranges for dedicated clusters and NAT egress (we'll provide per-region ranges and CIDR blocks)
- mTLS options for mutual-auth on callbacks and webhooks (supported via our private deployment routing)
- SDK quickstart and sample auth flow + example repo link for embeddings and reranking pattern

Action items / next steps:
1) I will share the VPC architecture diagram and the mutual action plan (attached).
2) Please share your internal network diagram and any IP ranges / NAT addresses you plan to use (Priya, can you send that?)
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Jonas (our lead solutions engineer) to walk through mTLS, egress/DNS, and auth. Jonas can own the runbook and any test harness setup.
4) We'll follow up with an updated MS/POC scope and timeline in HubSpot.

Proposed times for a 60-minute deep-dive (PST):
- Thu 2026-11-19 09:30–10:30
- Thu 2026-11-19 14:00–15:00
- Fri 2026-11-20 11:00–12:00

Let me know which works — if none, we'll coordinate.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-arch.png, mutual-action-plan.docx

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

From: Samir Khan <samir@finpay.com>

Date: 2026-11-17T17:46:00Z
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - post-call recap and next steps

Lauren — thanks for the recap, that all looks right. A few clarifying questions from our infra/security team so we can prepare before the deep-dive: 

1) mTLS: do you require mutual TLS for all inbound callbacks from Redwood, or can we opt for IP allowlist + token-based auth for the initial POC? If mTLS is required, what cert management patterns do you support (client cert rotation, CA trust chain)?

2) Egress & DNS: we prefer DNS resolution to stay in-VPC (i.e., use our internal DNS). Do you support private DNS zones or split-horizon DNS for the endpoint FQNs? Also, will callbacks require NAT egress to the internet or can they be routed to Redwood's VPC endpoint privately?

3) SDK + auth: For service-to-service auth, are you using short-lived JWTs exchanged via a signed assertion, or long-lived API keys scoped to environment? We prefer short-lived credentials. Also want to confirm sample code for embeddings ingestion (bulk) and a recommended reranker pattern (client-side vs server-side).

4) IP ranges: can you share the per-region CIDRs and whether you have a published list we can consume in automation?

5) Load: initial traffic expected ~50 requests/sec for embeddings ingestion with spikes to 200 rps during batch refreshes. Any config guidance (batch sizes, rate limits) you recommend up front?

Attached is our high-level network requirements doc (finpay-network-requirements.pdf). Happy to join either Thu slot (Nov 19 14:00 PST) — that works for Priya and me.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Director of Infrastructure | FinPay
samir@finpay.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@finpay.com>, Priya Desai <priya@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T01:12:00Z
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up & next steps

Samir — great questions. Quick answers and then I'll defer the deep technical details to Jonas during the deep-dive: 

1) mTLS: For initial POC we can support IP allowlist + token-based auth. For production we recommend mTLS for callbacks; we support automated cert rotation via our private deployment KMS integration or you can bring-your-own CA. We'll document rotation intervals and CA chain requirements in the runbook.

2) Egress & DNS: We support VPC interface endpoints and private DNS (split-horizon) when deployed in your VPC. Callbacks can remain over the private endpoint — no NAT egress required for the control plane if you choose interface endpoints and appropriate routing.

3) SDK & auth: We support short-lived JWTs exchanged via a signed assertion (recommended) and scoped service credentials. We also support scoped long-lived API keys for legacy systems. We'll provide sample code for bulk embeddings ingestion (Node/Python) and a server-side reranker pattern that executes the embedding similarity search server-side and calls a lightweight reranker model for the top-k. This minimizes client latency and data movement.

4) IP ranges: Attaching a spreadsheet of per-region CIDRs; we'll also publish a machine-readable JSON/CIDR endpoint you can hit for automation (expected ETA: 2 business days).

5) Load guidance: For 50 rps steady with 200 rps spikes, we recommend configuring batching windows to aggregate small requests (max_batch_tokens=4096) and using our async ingestion pipeline for bulk embeddings. We'll include default rate-limit thresholds and recommended autoscale headroom in the runbook.

Jonas — can you run the deep-dive and cover mTLS cert patterns, the published CIDR endpoint, and show a quick sample of the embeddings ingestion pipeline? Samir/Priya — confirmed for Thu Nov 19 14:00–15:00 PST. I've added the meeting in the calendar invite.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567) — I'll update the M.A.P. and scope after the session.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-arch.png, cidr-per-region.csv

Best,
Lauren
